title: Gibson Deletion: a novel application of isothermal in vitro recombination
author: Kalva, Boeke, et al.

steps.title: Prepare ISO assembly reagents
steps.instruction: Prepare the One‑step ISO assembly reagents (5X ISO Buffer and Gibson Reaction Master Mix) following the previously reported method.

steps.title: Anneal complementary oligonucleotides
steps.instruction: Mix 9 µL of 100 µM forward oligonucleotide, 9 µL of 100 µM reverse oligonucleotide, and 2 µL of 10X Annealing buffer (0.5 M Tris‑HCl pH 7.4, 0.1 M MgCl₂); heat at 95 °C for 5 min, then cool to room temperature by decreasing the temperature 5 °C every 30 s.

substeps.instruction: Add 9 µL forward oligo (100 µM) and 9 µL reverse oligo (100 µM) to a tube.
Add 2 µL 10X Annealing buffer (0.5 M Tris‑HCl pH 7.4, 0.1 M MgCl₂).
Heat the mixture at 95 °C for 5 min.
Cool to room temperature in 5 °C decrements, holding each step for 30 s.

steps.title: Set up Gibson assembly reaction
steps.instruction: Combine the DNA fragments to be assembled (PCR products, linearized plasmid, or single/double‑strand DNA) with 15 µL of Gibson Reaction Master Mix, adjusting with water or buffer so the total volume reaches 20 µL; ensure each DNA piece is added in equal molar amount, using a final concentration of 100 nM for single‑strand or annealed DNA pieces.

substeps.instruction: Add the desired DNA fragments (PCR products, linearized plasmid, etc.) at 100 nM concentration.
Add 15 µL Gibson Reaction Master Mix.
Add water or buffer as needed to bring the reaction to a final volume of 20 µL.
Verify that all DNA components are present in equal molar amounts.

steps.title: Incubate assembly at 50 °C
steps.instruction: Place the 20 µL reaction tube in a pre‑heated heat block set to 50 °C and incubate for 30 min.

steps.title: Transform assembled DNA into TOP10 cells
steps.instruction: Add 10 µL of the completed assembly reaction to 90 µL of TOP10 competent bacteria and follow the standard transformation procedure.
